review_notes: I read all of Defs.lean. It has no @[simp] lemmas, and its definitions are used by `simp [def]` throughout the TriangleInflation files. I grepped the sibling files (Finner, FinnerMeasure, Fan, Exponent, Defect, DefectLaw, Graph/*) for simp calls and for lemmas about bern, respMass, onLine, Rlaw and Q. I found no loops or competing rules, because no simp set is defined. All findings are about missing canonical simp lemmas that the downstream code re-derives or duplicates. I did not check that the proposed lemmas close the existing goals, since I can't run Lean. The `onLine` iff lemmas and the `Rlaw` marginal lemmas are the least likely to run into unforeseen simp-normal-form issues. The `bern` and `respMass` value lemmas hold by `rfl`.

findings.excerpt: def respMass (q : ℝ) : Bool → ℝ := fun b => if b then 1 - q else q
findings.problem: `respMass` has no simp lemmas for its two values. Every downstream use unfolds the whole definition with `simp [respMass]` and so exposes the `if b then …`. Finner.lean and FinnerMeasure.lean each define a private copy of `respMass q false = q` and `respMass q true = 1 - q`. Both are proved by `rfl`, so they are canonical rewrite rules. They are private and not simp, so other files cannot reuse them. Deterministic responses also have two separate copies of the same statement: `respMass_ite` (DoubleStar) and a private `respMass_det` (Rate).
findings.proposed_change: In Defs.lean, right after `respMass`, add `@[simp] theorem respMass_false (q : ℝ) : respMass q false = q := rfl` and `@[simp] theorem respMass_true (q : ℝ) : respMass q true = 1 - q := rfl`. Optionally add `respMass_sum : ∑ b, respMass q b = 1` as a simp lemma too. Delete the private copies `respMass_false`/`respMass_true` (Finner) and `respMassM_false`/`respMassM_true` (FinnerMeasure). Replace the `simp [respMass]` calls with plain `simp`, or `simp [respMass_false, respMass_true]`. Keep `respMass` itself irreducible to simp. Also move one of `respMass_ite` and `respMass_det` into Defs.lean and delete the other.
findings.benefit: Goals normalise to the numeric values `q` and `1 - q` instead of an `if` on a variable boolean. The duplicated helpers become one public lemma, and the many `simp [respMass]` unfoldings in Graph/Transport, FivePath, Soundness, Cycles and DoubleStar become robust rewrites that no longer depend on the definition's body.

evidence.excerpt: private lemma respMass_false (q : ℝ) : respMass q false = q := rfl
private lemma respMassM_false (q : ℝ) : respMass q false = q := rfl
respMass (if c then 0 else 1) b = if b = c then (1:ℝ) else 0

findings.excerpt: def bern (r : ℝ) : Bool → ℝ := fun b => if b then r else 1 - r
findings.problem: `bern` has no simp lemmas for `true` and `false`, even though the module docstring states `Bern(r)(true) = r`. Callers unfold it with `simp [bern]` or `simp only [Q, bern, …]`, as in Finner, Exponent, Defect and DefectLaw, so the generic `if b` appears and has to be case-split or re-simplified. `rootWeight` (lines 391–393) has the same issue: DefectLaw reaches `bern ε`/`bern s` only through `simp [rootWeight, bern]`, and there are no `rootWeight` lemmas for the `inl`/`inr` cases.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] theorem bern_true (r : ℝ) : bern r true = r := rfl` and `@[simp] theorem bern_false (r : ℝ) : bern r false = 1 - r := rfl`. Add `@[simp] theorem rootWeight_inl (t ε s) (c : Cell t) : rootWeight t ε s (Sum.inl c) = bern ε := rfl` and an `inr` analogue. Then use `simp [Q, bern_true, bern_false]` and plain `simp` in the callers, and drop `bern` from the unfold lists.
findings.benefit: The simp normal form of a Bernoulli weight at a concrete bit is the parameter itself or `1 - r`. Proofs that case-split on a bit no longer need `cases b <;> simp [bern] <;> linarith`. The unfold lists in `Q`/`Peps` computations shrink, and those computations stop depending on how `bern` is written.

evidence.excerpt: intro b; cases b <;> simp [bern] <;> linarith

findings.problem: `onLine` is `Bool`-valued, built from `&&` and `==`. Every user converts it to a statement about coordinates by repeating `simp only [onLine, Bool.and_eq_true, beq_iff_eq] at …`. Defect.lean `line_inter_ancestors` does this about a dozen times, and DefectLaw's `outputs_A`/`outputs_B`/`outputs_C` and `inDiagRegion` proofs do it too. There is no canonical Prop-level simp rule, so simp has to unfold the definition and rebuild the characterisation each time.
findings.proposed_change: After `onLine`, add `@[simp] theorem onLine_A_eq_true {t} (i j : Fin t) (c : Cell t) : onLine (.A i j) c = true ↔ c.1 = i ∧ c.2.1 = j`, with analogues for `B` (`c.1 = i ∧ c.2.2 = k`) and `C` (`c.2.1 = j ∧ c.2.2 = k`). Each should be provable by `simp [onLine]`. Callers then write `simp at hu`, or `rw [onLine_A_eq_true]`, without unfolding `onLine`. A `Prop`-valued `onLine` would also work.
findings.benefit: Hypotheses `onLine v c = true` normalise directly to coordinate equalities. The repeated three-lemma `simp only` incantations disappear, and the `onLine` unfold is no longer needed in `inDiagRegion`/`outputs` proofs.

evidence.excerpt: simp only [onLine, Bool.and_eq_true, beq_iff_eq] at hu
simp only [onLine, Bool.and_eq_true, beq_iff_eq] at hc
simp only [inDiagRegion, onLine, Bool.or_eq_true, Bool.and_eq_true, beq_iff_eq] at h1 h2

findings.excerpt: def Rlaw (p : ℝ) : ThreeBit → ℝ := fun w =>
findings.problem: The four evaluations `atom000 (Rlaw p) = p`, `margA (Rlaw p) = p`, `margB (Rlaw p) = p` and `margC (Rlaw p) = p` are used in several files. Each file re-proves them privately as `simp [atom000, Rlaw]`. Finner.lean has `R_atom`/`R_margA`/`R_margB`/`R_margC`, Fan.lean has `Rlaw_atom000`/`Rlaw_margA`/…, and FinnerMeasure.lean re-derives them locally as `have ha`/`hA`/`hB`/`hC`. None are public or simp, so the three call sites cannot share them.
findings.proposed_change: Define the four lemmas once in Defs.lean right after `Rlaw`, as `@[simp] theorem atom000_Rlaw (p : ℝ) : atom000 (Rlaw p) = p` and `margA_Rlaw`, `margB_Rlaw`, `margC_Rlaw` with the same right-hand side. Each is proved by `simp [atom000, Rlaw]` (or `margA` etc.). Delete the private copies in Finner, Fan and FinnerMeasure. Do the same for `Q`, stating `atom000 (Q ε r) = ε + (1 - ε) * (1 - r) ^ 3` and `margA (Q ε r) = ε + (1 - ε) * (1 - r)` as public lemmas. These currently exist as private `Q_atom`/`Q_margA`/… in Finner.lean, while Exponent.lean re-simps through `Peps, Q, bern`. These should be simp because the right-hand sides are in closed form with no unfolding of `atom000` or `margA`.
findings.benefit: `atom000`, `margA`, `margB`, `margC` stop being unfolded in each proof. They rewrite to their closed forms at `Rlaw p` and `Q ε r` in every file, and the duplicated lemmas are removed. This also makes it clear which side of the identity is the normal form.

private lemma Rlaw_margA (p : ℝ) : margA (Rlaw p) = p := by
have hA : margA (Rlaw p) = p := by simp [margA, Rlaw]
private lemma Q_margA (ε r : ℝ) : margA (Q ε r) = ε + (1 - ε) * (1 - r) := by
